study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modeling of brain MRI data identifies small subcortical volumes and associations with cognitive function in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD)

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To quantify regional subcortical brain volume anomalies in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) using normative modeling, assess the relative sensitivity and specificity of abnormal volumes in discriminating FASD from comparison group, and examine associations with cognitive function.

rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Unexpectedly, our participants (including those in the comparison group) demonstrated smaller than expected norm-corrected subcortical volumes (mean z-scores for those in the comparison group were negative as opposed to zero) in several regions including the left and right putamen and the right pallidum. These lower than expected z-scores could be due to differences in image acquisition and processing... Our preprocessing workflow included some steps (i.e., intensity normalization and gradient distortion correction using the proprietary Siemens gradient table), which may not have been performed in some of the datasets that informed the CentileBrain model. Additionally, while the HCP Minimal Preprocessing Pipelines are based around FreeSurfer version 6.0, many of the datasets used for CentileBrain were processed using either older or more recent versions of FreeSurfer (≤5.3 or ≥7.1) (Ge et al., 2024). Small differences across FreeSurfer versions, as well as the optional arguments used during processing, may have a significant impact on morphometric analyses and may explain the smaller than expected volumes we observed across both groups of participants in some subcortical structures (Filip et al., 2022)... Despite the systematic difference between our data and the normative data, we were still able to detect that the FASD group had smaller subcortical volumes than the comparison group.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Region-wise z-scores (M=0, SD=1) adjusted for age, sex, and ICV; atypically small volume defined as z ≤ -1.3 (equivalent to ≤10th percentile); atypically large volume defined as z ≥ 1.3 (equivalent to ≥90th percentile); total count of small/large volumes; sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and accuracy calculated for group discrimination
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper clearly describes the z-score calculation method, threshold definitions, and discrimination metrics. The 10th percentile threshold was chosen to mirror IOM diagnostic criteria for FASD.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: Z-scores (M = 0, SD = 1) were calculated for each of the 7 bilateral subcortical regions... Regional volume anomalies were characterized as 'small' (z-scores ≤ -1.3, equivalent to the 10th percentile) and 'large' (z-scores ≥ 1.3, equivalent to the 90th percentile). These thresholds for volumetric anomalies were selected in order to mirror IOM (Hoyme et al., 2016) diagnostic criteria for FASD with regard to head circumference and growth anomalies (e.g., height and weight) in which a threshold of ≤ 10th percentile is used... Using the total number of small regions, sensitivity (true positive rate), specificity (true negative rate), positive predictive value (probability of condition being present with a positive test), negative predictive value (probability of condition not being present with a negative test), and accuracy (overall probability of correct classification) were examined with regard to discriminating FASD and comparison participants.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis:
Answer: Independent samples t-tests compared regional subcortical volume z-scores between FASD and comparison groups (unadjusted p-values reported; effect sizes as Cohen's d). Chi-square tests and t-tests examined demographic differences. Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and accuracy calculated for discriminating groups based on small/large volume thresholds, both for total counts and region-specific. Exploratory uncorrected Pearson correlations examined relationships between regional volume z-scores and neurocognitive measures (Wechsler IQ, WISC-V/WAIS-IV Digit Span [working memory], NIH Toolbox Picture Sequence Memory Test [visual memory], D-KEFS Trail-Making Test Number-Letter Switching [executive function], D-KEFS Color-Word Interference Test Inhibition-Switching [cognitive flexibility]) conducted separately for FASD and comparison groups. Within FASD group, independent samples t-tests compared volumes by presence/absence of dysmorphic face, and Pearson correlations examined associations with height/weight percentile and sex differences in total extreme volumes.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed:
Answer: Group differences: FASD participants showed significantly lower mean z-scores than comparisons in 6 of 7 bilateral regions: bilateral thalami (left: d=0.48, p=0.029; right: d=0.52, p=0.017), bilateral caudate (left: d=0.85, p<0.001; right: d=0.90, p<0.001), left putamen (d=0.50, p=0.025), bilateral hippocampi (left: d=0.85, p<0.001; right: d=0.63, p=0.004), left amygdala (d=0.45, p=0.042), and right accumbens (d=0.51, p=0.019). Largest effects were in bilateral caudate and hippocampi. No significant differences in right putamen, bilateral pallidum, right amygdala, or left accumbens. FASD participants had greater mean number of small volumes (M=4.53, SD=3.13) versus comparisons (M=2.46, SD=2.30; t[83]=-3.53, p<0.001, d=-0.74). Overall, 89% of FASD versus 72% of comparisons had ≥1 small volume. Sensitivity/specificity: Bilateral putamen (left: 53% sensitivity, 62% specificity; right: 47% sensitivity, 67% specificity), bilateral hippocampi (left: 49% sensitivity, 82% specificity; right: 43% sensitivity, 87% specificity), right pallidum (45% sensitivity, 54% specificity), and right accumbens (40% sensitivity, 85% specificity) showed highest sensitivity. Bilateral caudate, right thalamus, and left amygdala were more specific (90-100% specificity) but less sensitive (17-36%). Brain-behavior associations: In FASD, positive correlations between bilateral caudate volumes and both IQ (left: r not specified but p<0.05; right: r not specified but p<0.05) and cognitive flexibility/D-KEFS Color-Word Interference Test Switching (bilateral, p<0.05). In comparisons, negative correlations between bilateral putamen/pallidum volumes and IQ, and between left putamen and D-KEFS Trail-Making Test Number-Letter Switching (all p<0.05). No significant associations found between subcortical volumes and facial dysmorphology, height/weight percentile, or sex within FASD group.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes:
Answer: Demonstrates application of pre-trained normative modeling tool (CentileBrain) to characterize individual-level subcortical brain anomalies in FASD. Authors suggest normative modeling offers benefits over traditional case-control approaches by characterizing within-group and within-individual variations (obscured by assumptions of within-group homogeneity) and reducing noise/variance due to age, sex, and motion. Study extends prior work showing whole-brain volume anomalies in FASD (Gimbel et al., 2024) to regional subcortical level. Findings suggest MRI-derived regional volume measures may have utility in identifying individuals with structural brain anomalies resulting from prenatal alcohol exposure and could potentially improve FASD diagnosis. Authors note direct MRI measurement previously showed greater sensitivity than head circumference (traditional FASD diagnostic proxy) and better accounted for variance in IQ. Study highlights importance of examining structural variability at individual level in FASD. Authors call for future research with larger samples to identify risk/protective factors associated with individual variation, network-based approaches modeling structural/functional connectivity, and validation in samples with broader clinical presentations and other neurodevelopmental conditions (ADHD, autism).
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative

Supporting Text: Recently published normative modeling tools based on large numbers of individuals provide a novel approach to quantifying variation in health-related variables (e.g., brain volumes) at the individual level... This approach offers benefits over using small, potentially unrepresentative comparison groups and case-control methodologies that assume within-group homogeneity (Rutherford et al., 2022)... brain volume centiles accounted for a greater proportion of variance in IQ than occipito-frontal head circumference (HC), which is typically used as a proxy of brain anomalies in FASD diagnosis (Hoyme et al. 2016). Brain volume centiles also demonstrated increased relative sensitivity to discriminating youth with FASD from the comparison group, demonstrating that direct measurement of the brain using MRI could potentially be used to improve FASD diagnosis... We demonstrate the value of normative MRI 'brain growth charts' in identifying and quantifying regional subcortical brain anomalies in youth with FASD at the individual level... findings suggest MRI may have utility in identifying individuals with structural brain anomalies resulting from PAE.

No explicit harmonization to address domain shift. Recruited sample may lack generalizability (single disorder focus, higher proportion White participants in comparison group, cognitively high-functioning FASD sample with mean IQ=93). Sample predominantly ARND (n=35) with few FAS (n=1) or PFAS (n=11). Focus only on subcortical ROIs; network-based approaches and cortical-subcortical connectivity not examined. Exploratory correlations uncorrected for multiple comparisons. No causal inferences can be drawn from brain-behavior associations.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Single-site study: data acquired at University of Minnesota on Siemens 3T Prisma with 32-channel head coil using HCP-D-like custom pulse sequences with automatic real-time motion detection and k-space line rejection/replacement. Processing: HCP Minimal Preprocessing Pipeline v4.0.1 (PreFreeSurfer and FreeSurfer v6.0 stages). Quality control: visual inspection by trained operators following ENIGMA protocols; Euler values assessed motion; exclusions: 3 comparison (aberrant FreeSurfer/failed boundary identification), 5 additional (3 comparison, 2 FASD) for motion/outlier. Final analyzed sample: 86 participants (47 FASD, 39 comparison). FASD diagnoses: 35 ARND, 11 PFAS, 1 FAS. Important technical note: Authors observed systematic z-score shifts (mean comparison group z-scores negative rather than zero) in several regions, attributed to domain shift between study preprocessing (HCP-aligned with intensity normalization and Siemens gradient distortion correction) and heterogeneous CentileBrain normative training data (87 datasets, 37,407 brains, FreeSurfer versions ≤5.3 to ≥7.1). Despite systematic differences, group discrimination (FASD vs comparison) was successful. Study part of CIFASD Phase 4 (2017-2022). Neuropsychological assessments: WISC-V/WAIS-IV (IQ, Digit Span), NIH Toolbox PSMT (visual memory), D-KEFS (Trail-Making, Color-Word Interference). 7 bilateral subcortical ROIs analyzed: amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus, accumbens. Left/right examined separately due to known structural asymmetries and prior FASD findings (e.g., lack of typical caudate asymmetry). Threshold for 'small' volume (z≤-1.3, ≤10th percentile) chosen to mirror IOM FASD diagnostic criteria for head circumference/growth. No other prenatal substance exposure (cannabis, opioids, cocaine, methamphetamine) confounding detected within PAE group (p>0.05 across regions).
